takeaway: Erb palsy: excessive neck-shoulder angle injures the superior brachial plexus (C5-C6, superior trunk), giving the waiter's tip position with loss of abduction, lateral rotation and elbow flexion.

question.text: A horse rider lands on his shoulder, stretching his neck. He loses shoulder abduction and lateral rotation, and elbow flexion and supination. Which roots are damaged?

lines.text: He landed with the neck stretched away from the shoulder.
That increased angle injures the superior part of the brachial plexus.
The C5 and C6 roots join to form the superior trunk.
lines.say: The C five and C six roots join to form the superior trunk.

lines.text: So he cannot abduct the shoulder, rotate it laterally, flex the elbow or supinate.
The arm hangs in the waiter's tip position.
So the damaged roots are C5 and C6.
lines.say: So the damaged roots are C five and C six.
